html:
The Gambia is the smallest country on the African mainland: a thin strip of land along both banks of the lower Gambia River in West Africa, surrounded by Senegal except at the sea.

The river was long a trade route. Its upper lands were part of the Mali Empire and later the Mandinka kingdom of Kaabu. Portuguese sailors arrived in 1455. From the 1600s the British held a fort on James Island, and the river became a channel of the Atlantic slave trade.

Britain founded Bathurst, now Banjul, in 1816 as a base against the slave trade. The colony's odd shape comes from deals with France, which held the land all around; the border was fixed in 1889. Groundnuts were the main crop.

  • 1965: independence under Dawda Jawara; a republic from 1970.
  • 1982 to 1989: a loose confederation with Senegal.
  • 1994: Yahya Jammeh took power in a coup and ruled until he lost the 2016 election.
sum: The Gambia is the smallest country on the African mainland: a thin strip of land along both banks of the lower Gambia River in West Africa, surrounded by Senegal except at the sea.
